To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the latent space of GANs can be interpreted as a Riemannian manifold, (ii) the metric tensor of this manifold is highly anisotrpoic and homogeneous, (iii) this metric allows us to perform efficient optimization in the image space (e.g., GAN inversion and image manipulation), (iv) the metric can be used to discover interpretable image axes, (v) this geometric interpretation unifies key previous GAN interpretability findings, and

(a) the latent space of a GAN can be understood by a Riemannian geometric framework that allows to identify interpretable axes and to invert the GAN to produce real-world images; (b) the latent space is anisotropic and homogeneous, which implies that the latent space of different GANs are similar, and that the same axes can be used for different tasks.
